item.title: Anti-Israel protesters who seized U. Washington building, caused $1M in damage, face charges
item.description: Thirty-three protesters who took over a University of Washington engineering building in May 2025, causing roughly $1 million in damage, are finally facing trespassing charges.

item.title: What do American students studying abroad think of Europe?
item.description: The College Fix's Simon Olech reports on American students' views of Europe from his study abroad program in Austria.

item.title: Bangor U. debate society refuses to debate conservative Reform UK, prompting backlash
item.description: Reform UK, a successor of the Brexit party, touts immigration controls, tax cuts, and deregulation.

item.title: NJ college revises policy after it banned funds to Christian Club
item.description: Atlantic Cape Community College revised its club funding policy after facing legal pressure regarding discrimination against religious and political student groups.

item.title: Florida bill would train professors to carry guns for campus emergencies
item.description: Opponents of Florida House Bill 757, which would train professors to carry concealed weapons on campus, argue it could create a dangerous "Wild West" environment.

item.title: U. Idaho professor wins $10 million defamation lawsuit after false murder accusations
item.description: Ashley Guillard could be required to pay out $10 million for her defamatory comments.

item.title: Yale senior thinks conservatives are dumb … well, dumber than liberals at least
item.description: Yale senior Milan Singh argues the predominance of liberal beliefs at Yale stems from innate intelligence, claiming studies link higher intelligence to left-wing ideologies. He disputes a peer's call for more conservative representation, asserting that the perception of ideological imbalance is justified. Critics, however, challenge his claims about intelligence and campus diversity.

item.title: UCSD vandalism: Pictures show moment Charlie Kirk assassinated with words he ‘had it coming’
Intersectional conundrum: Palestinian watermelon mural upsets black community
item.description: A pro-Palestinian mural in Richmond featuring a watermelon has sparked controversy in the black community, with leaders expressing concerns over its historical connotations. While the mural symbolizes Palestinian identity, some feel it unintentionally invokes stereotypes. Activists suggest modifications to bridge solidarity between the black liberation and Palestinian movements, emphasizing unity in their struggles.
